knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(V=\{1,\ldots,m\}\) index agents, let \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_m)\in X_1\times\cdots\times X_m\), and let agent \(i\) possess local objective, constraint, or observation data denoted by \(\mathcal I_i\). Let \(\mathcal G=(V,E)\) specify permitted peer-to-peer information exchange.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-agent, finite-dimensional taxonomy of deterministic optimization models; the classification concerns mathematical ownership and coupling, not a particular algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A distributed optimization model is a tuple \(\mathfrak M=(V,(X_i)_{i\in V},(\mathcal I_i)_{i\in V},F,\mathcal C,\mathcal A)\) defining \(\inf_{x\in\mathcal C}F(x)\), where each \(\mathcal I_i\) is initially available only to agent \(i\), \(\mathcal C\subseteq\prod_iX_i\), and \(\mathcal A\) specifies admissible information exchanges. Its taxonomy is the classification by (i) objective ownership, including separable \(F(x)=\sum_i f_i(x_i)\) and shared-decision \(F(z)=\sum_i f_i(z)\); (ii) decision ownership, shared or block-partitioned; (iii) coupling, such as agreement, aggregate, flow, or general constraints; and (iv) coordination architecture, centralized, decentralized, or hierarchical.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A distributed optimization model specifies the agents, their decision domains and private information, the global objective and feasible set, and the allowed communication architecture. Models are classified independently by who owns objective information, whether the decision is shared or partitioned, which constraints prevent independent local solution, and how coordination information may be exchanged.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathfrak M=(V,(X_i)_i,(\mathcal I_i)_i,F,\mathcal C,\mathcal A)\) is distributed precisely when the global problem \(\inf_{x\in\mathcal C}F(x)\) is defined from agent-indexed information with nontrivial locality restrictions encoded by \(\mathcal A\); its model class is determined by objective ownership, variable ownership, coupling, and coordination structure.
equivalent_formulations_latex: A centralized finite-dimensional problem becomes a distributed model after specifying a decomposition of its data into \((\mathcal I_i)_i\) and an information-access relation \(\mathcal A\); the algebraic problem alone does not determine the distributed taxonomy.
special_cases_latex: Shared-decision sum models use one \(z\in X\) and local terms \(f_i(z)\).
Partitioned-variable models use \(x_i\in X_i\) and couple the blocks through \(F\) or \(\mathcal C\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If both \(F(x)=\sum_i f_i(x_i)\) and \(\mathcal C=\prod_i C_i\), the mathematical problem separates into independent local problems; distribution then supplies parallelism but no optimization coupling.
boundary_notes: Communication timing, failures, privacy, and stochastic sampling are additional model coordinates not fixed by this definition.

children.title: Distributed Objective and Variable Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Canonical ways to distribute objectives, variables, constraints, and observations.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(V=\{1,\ldots,m\}\) be a finite agent set. Agent \(i\) controls \(x_i\in X_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_i}\) and initially knows local data \(\mathcal I_i\). Write \(x=(x_i)_{i\in V}\in X:=\prod_iX_i\), and let \(\mathcal G=(V,E)\) describe allowed communication.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional deterministic formulation allowing shared or partitioned decisions, extended-valued objectives, and arbitrary global coupling constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A distributed optimization problem is \(p^\star=\inf\{F(x;\mathcal I_1,\ldots,\mathcal I_m):x\in\mathcal C\subseteq X\}\), together with the ownership rule that agent \(i\) initially accesses only \(\mathcal I_i\) and an admissible communication structure \(\mathcal G\). The problem is genuinely coupled when it cannot be represented simultaneously as \(F(x)=\sum_iF_i(x_i;\mathcal I_i)\) and \(\mathcal C=\prod_i\mathcal C_i\) without introducing shared quantities. A solution is any \(x^\star\in\mathcal C\) satisfying \(F(x^\star)=p^\star\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A distributed optimization problem is a global minimization problem whose objective or feasible set is assembled from information initially divided among agents, accompanied by a rule limiting information exchange. It is genuinely coupled if the objective and feasible set cannot both be decomposed into independent agent-local factors. A solution is a feasible decision attaining the global infimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathcal C}F(x;\mathcal I_1,\ldots,\mathcal I_m)\) is a solution, while the tuple consisting of this optimization problem, local information ownership, and \(\mathcal G\) is the distributed problem specification.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Local constraints may be encoded by indicator functions: replacing \(F\) by \(F+\sum_i\iota_{C_i}(x_i)\) converts \(x_i\in C_i\) into extended-valued objective terms while leaving nonlocal constraints explicit.
special_cases_latex: For a shared variable \(z\), \(\min_{z\in C}\sum_i f_i(z)\) distributes objective data.
For block variables, \(\min_{x_i\in X_i}\sum_i f_i(x_i)\) subject to \(Ax=b\) distributes decisions but couples feasibility.
immediate_consequences_latex: If no minimizer attains \(p^\star\), the problem remains well-defined but its solution set is empty.
boundary_notes: Distributed execution is not implied merely by writing an objective as a sum; locality and admissible information access must also be specified.
Convexity, smoothness, synchrony, and stochasticity are not imposed.

children.title: Shared-Decision Sum Optimization
children.top_down_role: Agent-local objective components coupled through a common decision.

knowledge_statements.title: Shared-Decision Sum Optimization
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Agents contribute separate objective terms but optimize one common decision; a solution minimizes their summed objective over the shared feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A shared-decision sum optimization problem for \(m\) agents is
\[
\operatorname*{minimize}_{x\in X}\;F(x):=\sum_{i=1}^{m} f_i(x).
\]
The same variable \(x\) occurs in every summand, while agent \(i\) owns or evaluates \(f_i\). Feasibility restrictions may be encoded by \(X\) or by assigning value \(+\infty\) outside an agent-local domain. Its solution set is \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}F(x)\).
assumptions_latex: \(m\in\mathbb{N}\) agents share a decision space \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\).
Each agent owns an extended-real objective \(f_i:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical finite-agent shared-variable formulation; convexity is not part of the definition.

notation.meaning: Single decision shared by all agents.

children.title: Partitioned-Variable Optimization
children.top_down_role: Distinct variable blocks assigned to different agents.

knowledge_statements.title: Partitioned-Variable Optimization
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each agent controls a distinct variable block, while the objective or feasible set may still couple blocks across agents.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A partitioned-variable optimization problem assigns distinct blocks \(x_i\in X_i\) to agents and has the form
\[
\operatorname*{minimize}_{x=(x_1,\ldots,x_m)\in C}\;\Phi(x_1,\ldots,x_m),
\]
where \(C\subseteq X_1\times\cdots\times X_m\). The ownership partition concerns variables, not necessarily separability: \(\Phi\) may couple several blocks, and \(C\) need not equal the full product. When \(\Phi(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)\), only the constraints can couple agents.
assumptions_latex: \(m\in\mathbb{N}\) and \(X=X_1\times\cdots\times X_m\), with \(X_i\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{d_i}\).
Agent \(i\) owns block \(x_i\in X_i\), and \(C\subseteq X\) is the joint feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^\star=(x_1^\star,\ldots,x_m^\star)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}\Phi(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block-distributed model, allowing both separable and coupled objectives or constraints.

notation.meaning: Decision block owned by agent i.

children.title: Distributed Data-Parallel Optimization
children.top_down_role: Shared model variables paired with partitioned observations.

knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Data-Parallel Optimization
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Observations are partitioned among agents, but every shard contributes loss terms for the same shared model parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Distributed data-parallel optimization is the shared-model problem
\[
\operatorname*{minimize}_{w\in W}\;r(w)+\sum_{i=1}^{m}L_i(w),
\qquad L_i(w):=\sum_{z\in D_i}\ell(w;z),
\]
where agent \(i\) stores the observation shard \(D_i\), but every local loss is evaluated at the same model parameter \(w\). Dividing the entire objective by the positive constant \(|D|\) does not change its minimizers; other sample-weighting conventions define the corresponding weighted empirical-risk objective.
assumptions_latex: \(m\in\mathbb{N}\), and the finite dataset \(D\) is partitioned as \(D=\bigsqcup_{i=1}^m D_i\).
All agents optimize the same parameter \(w\in W\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\).
The sample loss is \(\ell:W\times D\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), and the optional global regularizer is \(r:W\to(-\infty,+\infty]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(w^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{w\in W}\left(r(w)+\sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{z\in D_i}\ell(w;z)\right)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-sample empirical-risk form with horizontally partitioned observations.

notation.meaning: Data shard stored by agent i.

children.title: Distributed Feasibility Coupling Models
children.top_down_role: Constraints or feasible-set information held locally by agents.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(V=\{1,\ldots,m\}\), let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), and let agent \(i\) own a nonempty set \(C_i\subseteq X\), or equivalently local constraint functions defining that set.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic common-variable feasibility and constrained optimization; sets may be nonconvex unless convexity is stated separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A distributed feasibility coupling model asks for \(z\in C:=\bigcap_{i=1}^mC_i\), where the description or membership oracle of \(C_i\) is initially available only to agent \(i\). With an objective \(F\), the associated constrained problem is \(\inf_{z\in\cap_iC_i}F(z)\). If \(C_i=\{z:g_i(z)\le0,\ h_i(z)=0\}\), feasibility means \(g_i(z)\le0\) and \(h_i(z)=0\) for every agent \(i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A distributed feasibility coupling model gives each agent private information about one feasible set and requires one shared decision to satisfy every local set simultaneously. An objective may be optimized over the resulting intersection, but the defining coupling is the global intersection of locally described constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The global feasible set is exactly \(C=\bigcap_iC_i\), and a feasible solution is any \(z\) satisfying every locally held membership condition.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Using indicator functions, \(z\in\bigcap_iC_i\) is equivalent to minimizing \(\sum_i\iota_{C_i}(z)\) with optimal value \(0\) when the intersection is nonempty.
With local copies, feasibility is \(x_i\in C_i\) and \(x_1=\cdots=x_m\).
special_cases_latex: Distributed linear feasibility uses \(C_i=\{z:A_iz\le b_i\}\).
Distributed convex feasibility requires every \(C_i\) to be closed and convex.
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(\cap_iC_i=\varnothing\), the feasibility problem has no solution and the indicator-sum objective is identically infinite at every common feasible candidate.
boundary_notes: Aggregate constraints involving distinct \(x_i\) are not intersection models unless reformulated with an appropriate product-space lifting.
No regularity, projection accessibility, or constraint qualification is part of the definition.

notation.meaning: feasible set described by agent i
extended-valued indicator of the set C_i

knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Feasibility Coupling Model
Local Constraint Ownership
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each agent owns a membership constraint on the shared decision; global feasibility requires satisfying every owned constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Local constraint ownership means that agent \(i\) stores, evaluates, or enforces the predicate \(x\in C_i\) for a common candidate \(x\in X\). The distributed constraint system is
\[
x\in C_i\quad(i=1,\ldots,m),
\]
and therefore its global feasible set is \(C:=\bigcap_{i=1}^m C_i\). Ownership specifies information placement; it does not imply that \(C_i\) is private, convex, or independent of the other sets.
assumptions_latex: \(m\in\mathbb{N}\) agents share a decision space \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\).
For each \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), agent \(i\) is assigned a local feasible set \(C_i\subseteq X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\) is globally feasible exactly when \(x\in\bigcap_{i=1}^m C_i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-based ownership of constraints on a shared decision.

notation.meaning: Constraint set whose membership agent i can evaluate.

knowledge_statements.title: Intersections of Local Feasible Sets
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The globally feasible decisions are precisely the intersection of all agent-local feasible sets; convex local sets yield a convex, possibly empty, intersection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For local feasible sets \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\subseteq X\), simultaneous satisfaction is represented by
\[
C:=\bigcap_{i=1}^{m}C_i
 =\{x\in X: x\in C_i\text{ for all }i=1,\ldots,m\}.
\]
Thus a distributed feasibility problem asks for any \(x\in C\), and an optimization problem with local constraints minimizes its objective over \(C\). If every \(C_i\) is convex, then \(C\) is convex; the intersection may nevertheless be empty.
assumptions_latex: \(C_i\subseteq X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C=\bigcap_{i=1}^m C_i=\{x\in X:x\in C_i\text{ for every }i\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact set representation for conjunctive local constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Coupled Feasibility Relations
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Joint feasibility can be defined by relations involving selected groups of agent variables, rather than by independent constraints on single blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A coupled feasibility system on \(X:=\prod_{i=1}^m X_i\) is specified by relations \(R_e\subseteq\prod_{i\in S_e}X_i\), where each \(S_e\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\). Its joint feasible set is
\[
C:=\left\{x\in X:(x_i)_{i\in S_e}\in R_e\text{ for every }e\right\}.
\]
A relation is genuinely coupling when membership cannot be expressed as independent conditions on each participating block. Pairwise agreement, network balance, and shared-budget constraints are special cases.
assumptions_latex: Agent decisions satisfy \(x_i\in X_i\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{d_i}\).
For each relation \(e\), \(R_e\subseteq\prod_{i\in S_e}X_i\) involves the agent subset \(S_e\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in C\iff (x_i)_{i\in S_e}\in R_e\) for every relation \(e\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General finite relational model encompassing pairwise, hyperedge, and global constraints.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The relational formulation is mathematically plausible, but the domain over which e ranges is not introduced. More importantly, the cited general chapter opening does not specifically support the hyperedge-style family of relations or the stated characterization of genuine coupling. A source with a precise locator for factor-graph, hypergraph, or multi-block relational constraints is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility Conflict Boundaries
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The minimum worst distance to local sets measures conflict; a positive value certifies infeasibility, while zero certifies feasibility when the infimum is attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the feasibility-conflict radius by
\[
\rho:=\inf_{x\in X}\max_{1\le i\le m}d(x,C_i),
\qquad d(x,C_i):=\inf_{y\in C_i}\|x-y\|.
\]
For finitely many nonempty closed sets, \(\rho=0\) whenever their intersection is nonempty. Conversely, if the infimum is attained, then \(\rho=0\) implies \(x\in\bigcap_{i=1}^m C_i\) at a minimizer. Hence \(\rho>0\) certifies a positive incompatibility margin, while nonattainment must be excluded before treating \(\rho=0\) as feasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(C_i\subseteq X\) are nonempty closed sets in a normed space \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho=0\) exactly when \(\bigcap_{i=1}^m C_i\neq\varnothing\); if the intersection is empty, \(\rho\) quantifies best attainable worst local violation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metric boundary between consistent and inconsistent finite local-set systems.

notation.meaning: Distance from x to local feasible set i.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The conclusion_latex incorrectly states an unconditional equivalence between rho=0 and nonempty intersection, whereas the statement correctly notes that the reverse implication needs attainment or another sufficient compactness/coercivity condition. The cited distributed-optimization chapter opening does not specifically support this conflict-radius definition or its boundary characterization, so an authoritative source is required before selecting and repairing the precise hypothesis set.

children.title: Distributed Coupling Models
children.top_down_role: Structures that prevent independent solution of agent-local problems.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(x=(x_1,ldots,x_m)\in X=\prod_iX_i\), and consider \(\inf_{x\in\mathcal C}\Phi(x)\). Each block and its local data are assigned to an agent.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic taxonomy of deterministic finite-dimensional coupling, independent of communication protocol or solution method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The coupling structure is the collection of objective and feasibility relations whose scopes contain variables or information owned by more than one agent. Formally, write \(\Phi=\sum_{a\in\mathcal F}\phi_a(x_{S_a})\) and \(\mathcal C=\{x:c_b(x_{T_b})\in K_b,\ b\in\mathcal B\}\), where \(S_a,T_b\subseteq V\). A factor or constraint is coupling when its scope has cardinality greater than one; agreement constraints, aggregate relations, network-flow conservation, and general cross-block constraints are canonical coupling types.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coupling structure is the set of objective factors and constraints that jointly involve information or decision blocks belonging to multiple agents. It can be represented by the scopes of objective factors and constraint relations. Agreement, aggregate resource, network-flow, and general cross-block constraints are standard coupling types.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The model is uncoupled exactly when every objective and constraint scope is a singleton and the feasible set factors by agent; otherwise the nonsingleton scopes define its coupling structure.
equivalent_formulations_latex: A bipartite factor graph with variable vertices \(i\in V\) and factor vertices \(\mathcal F\cup\mathcal B\) represents the same structure, with an edge whenever an agent index belongs to a factor's scope.
special_cases_latex: Agreement coupling has factors enforcing \(x_i=x_j\).
Aggregate coupling has a relation on \(\sum_iA_ix_i\).
Flow coupling uses node-edge incidence relations.
immediate_consequences_latex: If the factor graph has several connected components, the mathematical problem decomposes across those components, subject to any omitted global terms.
boundary_notes: Statistical dependence between data sources is not by itself an optimization coupling unless it appears in the objective or feasible relations.
Communication edges need not coincide with coupling-factor edges.

target set or cone for constraint b

children.title: Replicated-Decision Agreement Coupling
children.top_down_role: Agreement coupling among replicated decision variables.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal G=(V,E)\) be an undirected graph with \(V=\{1,\ldots,m\}\). Agent \(i\) holds a replica \(x_i\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_m)\in\mathbb R^{mn}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact deterministic agreement over an undirected graph; approximate, directed, and time-varying agreement are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Replicated-decision agreement coupling is the feasible subspace \(\mathcal C_{\mathcal G}=\{x:x_i=x_j\text{ for every }\{i,j\}\in E\}\). If \(B\) is an oriented node-edge incidence matrix, then \(\mathcal C_{\mathcal G}=\ker(B^\top\otimes I_n)\). When \(\mathcal G\) is connected, this equals the consensus subspace \(\{\mathbf1_m\otimes z:z\in\mathbb R^n\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Agreement coupling gives every agent a replica of one decision and constrains replicas at adjacent graph vertices to be equal. The same constraint is the null space of the graph incidence operator. On a connected graph, edgewise agreement is exactly global consensus on one vector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in\mathcal C_{\mathcal G}\) if and only if \((B^\top\otimes I_n)x=0\); for connected \(\mathcal G\), this holds if and only if there exists \(z\in\mathbb R^n\) with \(x_i=z\) for every \(i\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: With graph Laplacian \(L=BB^\top\), agreement is equivalently \((L\otimes I_n)x=0\).
special_cases_latex: A complete graph directly imposes all pairwise equalities.
A spanning tree supplies sufficient edge equalities for global agreement.
immediate_consequences_latex: For a graph with \(q\) connected components, feasible replicas may take one independent common value per component.
boundary_notes: For directed graphs, the appropriate incidence or Laplacian condition depends on orientation and connectivity conventions.
Penalty terms such as \(\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}\|x_i-x_j\|^2\) encourage agreement but do not impose exact coupling at finite weight.
review_flags: The precise incidence-matrix equivalence could not be tied to an inspected source locator.
knowledge_statements.title: Replicated-Decision Agreement Coupling
Consensus Coupling
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Consensus requires neighboring local decisions to agree; on a connected graph this is equivalent to agreement among all agents.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Choose an orientation of \(E\), let \(\bar B\in\mathbb{R}^{|E|\times m}\) be the incidence matrix, and set \(B:=\bar B\otimes I_d\). Consensus coupling is the condition
\[
Bx=0,
\]
which is equivalent to \(x_i=x_j\) for every edge \(\{i,j\}\in E\). If \(G\) is connected, these edge equalities are equivalent to global agreement \(x_1=\cdots=x_m\); if \(G\) is disconnected, they impose agreement only within each connected component.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is an undirected graph with \(V=\{1,\ldots,m\}\).
Each agent holds \(x_i\in\mathbb{R}^d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(G\) is connected, then \(Bx=0\iff x_1=\cdots=x_m\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Undirected connected-graph consensus characterized by incidence constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Local-Copy Replication
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A shared decision is lifted to one copy per agent, with equality constraints making the replicated and original formulations equivalent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Local-copy replication replaces the shared variable \(z\) by one copy \(x_i\in Z\) per agent and rewrites
\[
\operatorname*{minimize}_{z\in Z}\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(z)
\quad\text{as}\quad
\operatorname*{minimize}_{x_1,\ldots,x_m\in Z}\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)
\quad\text{subject to}\quad x_1=\cdots=x_m.
\]
The mapping \(z\mapsto(z,\ldots,z)\) is a bijection between feasible decisions of the original problem and agreement-feasible replicated decisions, preserving objective values.
assumptions_latex: A shared-variable problem has decision \(z\in Z\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) and local terms \(f_i(z)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The replicated formulation is equivalent to the original when \(x_1=\cdots=x_m\), with \(z=x_i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact lifting of a shared decision into agent-local copies.

knowledge_statements.title: Copy-to-Global Coupling
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every local copy is constrained to equal one global variable; eliminating that variable recovers ordinary all-agent consensus.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Copy-to-global coupling introduces \(z\in\mathbb{R}^d\) and imposes
\[
x_i-z=0\quad(i=1,\ldots,m).
\]
Equivalently, for the stacked vector \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_m)\), the constraint is \(x-\mathbf{1}_m\otimes z=0\). Eliminating \(z\) yields \(x_1=\cdots=x_m\), while any consensual tuple determines the unique value \(z=x_i\). This representation centralizes agreement through a star-shaped coupling variable.
assumptions_latex: Each agent has a local copy \(x_i\in\mathbb{R}^d\).
A global coordination variable satisfies \(z\in\mathbb{R}^d\).

knowledge_statements.title: Agreement-Violation Structure
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Edgewise copy differences form a consensus residual, whose squared norm equals the graph-Laplacian disagreement energy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\bar B\) be an oriented incidence matrix and define the agreement residual
\[
r:=(\bar B\otimes I_d)x.
\]
The block of \(r\) associated with an oriented edge \((i,j)\) equals \(x_i-x_j\), up to the chosen orientation. Hence \(r=0\) exactly when every edge agrees. Moreover, with \(L:=\bar B^T\bar B\),
\[
\|r\|_2^2=x^T(L\otimes I_d)x=\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}\|x_i-x_j\|_2^2,
\]
so Laplacian energy is a nonnegative scalar measure of agreement violation.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is an oriented undirected graph.
The stacked local decision is \(x\in(\mathbb{R}^d)^m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r=0\) exactly characterizes edgewise agreement, and \(\|r\|_2^2=x^T(L\otimes I_d)x\).

knowledge_statements.title: Aggregate Resource Coupling
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Agents make separate decisions, but their summed resource use or contribution must satisfy a common capacity or balance relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Aggregate resource coupling joins otherwise separable decisions through a shared relation such as
\[
\sum_{i=1}^{m}A_i x_i\le b
\quad\text{or}\quad
\sum_{i=1}^{m}A_i x_i=b,
\qquad x_i\in X_i.
\]
The inequality is interpreted componentwise and models common capacities; the equality models conservation or balance. Although each contribution \(A_i x_i\) is locally determined, feasibility depends on their aggregate, so the joint feasible set generally is not a Cartesian product of agent-local feasible sets.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The decisions are jointly feasible when \(\sum_{i=1}^m A_i x_i\le b\), or when \(\sum_{i=1}^m A_i x_i=b\) in the balance form.

knowledge_statements.title: Consensus Optimization
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Agents minimize the sum of local objectives while graph constraints force all local decision copies to agree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a connected undirected graph. Agent \(i\in V\) owns a proper function \(f_i:\mathbb R^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and a local copy \(x_i\in\mathbb R^d\). knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_i=x_j\) on every edge if and only if \(x_i=x\) for some common \(x\) and all \(i\in V\).

children.top_down_role: Problems with distributed primal, dual, or adversarial variables.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and \(Y\subseteq\mathbb R^p\) be nonempty strategy sets. Agents possess local payoff components \(L_i:X\times Y\to\mathbb R\), and \(L(x,y)=\sum_iw_iL_i(x,y)\) with \(w_i>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic two-sided zero-sum minimax and saddle formulations with distributed payoff information or distributed primal/dual blocks; existence of a saddle point is not presumed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A distributed adversarial problem is \(\inf_{x\in X}\sup_{y\in Y}L(x,y)\), where evaluation or ownership of \(L\), \(x\), or \(y\) is partitioned among agents. A saddle solution is a pair \((x^\star,y^\star)\in X\times Y\) satisfying \(L(x^\star,y)\le L(x^\star,y^\star)\le L(x,y^\star)\) for every \(x\in X\) and \(y\in Y\). Block-distributed variants take \(x=(x_i)_i\), \(y=(y_j)_j\), with feasibility or payoff terms coupling those blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A distributed adversarial problem is a minimax problem in which payoff information or primal and adversarial variables are divided among agents. A saddle solution simultaneously prevents the maximizing side from improving against the chosen primal strategy and the minimizing side from improving against the chosen adversarial strategy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The family is defined by the distributed minimax relation \(\inf_{x\in X}\sup_{y\in Y}L(x,y)\); its saddle-solution set consists exactly of pairs satisfying the two-sided inequality for all feasible opposing strategies.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For differentiable convex-concave \(L\), the associated saddle operator is \(F(x,y)=(\nabla_xL(x,y),-\nabla_yL(x,y))\), yielding a variational-inequality representation when the required regularity holds.
special_cases_latex: Distributed empirical games use \(L=m^{-1}\sum_iL_i\).
Lagrangian saddle problems use \(L(x,y)=f(x)+\langle y,g(x)\rangle\) with dual or multiplier variables distributed or coordinated across agents.
immediate_consequences_latex: The saddle inequalities imply equality of the lower and upper values at \((x^\star,y^\star)\); without such a pair, the minimax problem remains defined but has no saddle solution.
boundary_notes: General-sum multi-player games are not included in this two-sided zero-sum definition.
Convexity-concavity, compactness, and minimax interchange are additional hypotheses, not defining properties.
No accessible source supported the full distributed family and its block variants.

knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Adversarial Problem Family
Distributed Saddle Models
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Agents contribute local convex-concave payoffs while network constraints coordinate their primal and dual copies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let agent \(i\in V\) own a function \(\Phi_i:X\times Y\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) that is convex in \(x\in X\) and concave in \(y\in Y\). A consensus-form distributed saddle model is \[\min_{(x_i)}\max_{(y_i)}\ \sum_{i\in V}\Phi_i(x_i,y_i)\quad\text{subject to}\quad x_i=x_j,\quad y_i=y_j\quad((i,j)\in E).\] If the undirected graph \(G=(V,E)\) is connected, feasible copies equal common variables \((x,y)\), and the model becomes \(\min_{x\in X}\max_{y\in Y}\sum_i\Phi_i(x,y)\).
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is finite, undirected, and connected.
Every \(\Phi_i\) is convex in its primal argument and concave in its dual argument.
All agents use the common spaces \(X\) and \(Y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Consensus reduces the distributed model to \(\min_{x\in X}\max_{y\in Y}\sum_{i\in V}\Phi_i(x,y)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Agents collectively solve a convex-concave saddle problem with coordinated primal and dual variables.

notation.meaning: Agent i's local dual or adversarial variable.

knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Minimax Models
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Agents collectively minimize against an adversary when each agent knows only one weighted, real-valued payoff component; local copies of the shared decisions may be coordinated through network consensus.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m\in\mathbb{N}\), let \(X\) and \(Y\) be nonempty convex sets, and let agent \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\) hold a function \(\phi_i:X\times Y\to\mathbb{R}\). Given weights \(w_i>0\) satisfying \(\sum_{i=1}^{m}w_i=1\), a distributed minimax model is
\[\min_{x\in X}\max_{y\in Y}\;\Phi(x,y),\qquad \Phi(x,y)=\sum_{i=1}^{m}w_i\phi_i(x,y).\]
Agent \(i\) can evaluate only its local component or an associated oracle. A distributed representation may introduce copies \((x_i,y_i)\) and impose \(x_i=x_j\) and \(y_i=y_j\) on communication edges.
assumptions_latex: \(m\in\mathbb{N}\) agents communicate over a prescribed network.
\(X\) and \(Y\) are nonempty convex sets.
Each \(\phi_i\) is convex in \(x\) and concave in \(y\) when a convex–concave model is intended.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Phi=\sum_{i=1}^{m}w_i\phi_i\) defines a distributed minimax problem with shared primal and adversarial decisions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-agent minimax model with locally held payoff components and shared primal and adversarial variables.

notation.meaning: payoff component held by agent i

knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Variable Ownership
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ownership maps assign every primal and dual block to one or more agents; copies of a shared block represent one variable exactly when they agree across a connected replica communication graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P\) and \(Q\) index the primal and dual coordinate blocks of \(x=(x^{(p)})_{p\in P}\) and \(y=(y^{(q)})_{q\in Q}\), and let \(V=\{1,\ldots,m\}\) be the agent set. Ownership maps \(o_x:P\to 2^V\setminus\{\varnothing\}\) and \(o_y:Q\to 2^V\setminus\{\varnothing\}\) assign each block to the agents permitted to update or store it. For a shared block replicated on a set \(R\subseteq V\), stack its copies as \(z_R=(z_i)_{i\in R}\). If the communication subgraph on \(R\) is connected and has oriented node-edge incidence matrix \(B_R\), consistency is
\[(B_R^{\mathsf T}\otimes I)z_R=0.\]
Thus agents update owned blocks from local information, and the replicated copies of a shared block represent one variable exactly when this consensus equation holds.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) and \(Q\) are the primal and dual block-index sets, and \(V=\{1,\ldots,m\}\) is the agent set.
Every coordinate block has at least one owner.
The communication subgraph for every replicated shared block is connected.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((B_R^{\mathsf T}\otimes I)z_R=0\) makes all copies of a shared block on \(R\) equal.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ownership representation for distributed saddle formulations using local blocks, replicated shared variables, and consensus constraints.

notation.meaning: oriented node-edge incidence matrix of the replica subgraph
stack of copies of a shared block on the replica set R

knowledge_statements.title: Adversarial Coordination Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coordination regime records which primal and adversarial agents update, in what order, and whether their neighbor information is current or delayed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For local states \(z_i^k=(x_i^k,y_i^k)\), an adversarial coordination regime specifies activation sets \(S_k^x,S_k^y\), the information timestamp \(\tau_{ij}(k)\le k\), and the order of primal, adversarial, and mixing operations. The regime is simultaneous when \(S_k^x=S_k^y\) and both updates use round-\(k\) states; alternating when one update uses the other variable's newly computed value; and delayed when some received value is \(z_j^{\tau_{ij}(k)}\) with \(\tau_{ij}(k)<k\). It is bounded-delay when \(0\le k-\tau_{ij}(k)\le D\) uniformly.
assumptions_latex: Iterations are indexed by \(k\in\mathbb{N}\).
Each active agent uses only locally available or received states.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((S_k^x,S_k^y,\tau(k))\) distinguishes simultaneous, alternating, and bounded-delay adversarial coordination.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous, alternating, and delayed regimes for coordinating distributed primal and adversarial updates.

notation.meaning: active primal and adversarial agent sets at round k
timestamp of agent j's state used by agent i

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(m\ge 2\), let \(\mathcal H_i\) be real Hilbert spaces, and set \(\mathcal H=\prod_{i=1}^m\mathcal H_i\). Agent \(i\) controls \(x_i\in\mathcal H_i\). Let \(A_i:\mathcal H_i\rightrightarrows\mathcal H_i\) be set-valued local operators and let \(B_i:\mathcal H\to\mathcal H_i\) describe coupling among agents.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This definition covers deterministic distributed equilibrium systems expressible as a product-space monotone inclusion; monotonicity is part of the named family, whereas maximality and solvability are additional analytical assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The distributed equilibrium problem associated with \((A_i,B_i)_{i=1}^m\) is to find \(x^\star=(x_1^\star,\ldots,x_m^\star)\in\mathcal H\) such that \[0\in A_i x_i^\star+B_i(x^\star)\quad\text{for every }i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}.\] Equivalently, with \(A=\prod_{i=1}^m A_i\) and \(B(x)=(B_1(x),\ldots,B_m(x))\), its solution set is \[\operatorname{zer}(A+B)=\{x\in\mathcal H:0\in A(x)+B(x)\}.\] The problem belongs to the monotone distributed equilibrium family when every \(A_i\) and the product-space coupling operator \(B\) are monotone on their respective domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A distributed monotone-inclusion equilibrium problem has one decision component per agent. A solution is a product-space vector whose component at every agent satisfies the local set-valued equilibrium condition after the network coupling term is added. Collecting the local operators and coupling maps produces the single product-space inclusion zero in A plus B.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Sol}=\{x\in\mathcal H:(\forall i)\ 0\in A_i x_i+B_i(x)\}=\operatorname{zer}(A+B)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(A_i=\partial f_i\) and \(B_i(x)=\nabla_{x_i}\Phi_i(x)\), the conditions become \(0\in\partial f_i(x_i^\star)+\nabla_{x_i}\Phi_i(x^\star)\) for all \(i\).

If \(A=N_C\) for a nonempty closed convex set \(C\subseteq\mathcal H\), the inclusion is the variational inequality \(\langle B(x^\star),x-x^\star\rangle\ge0\) for every \(x\in C\), provided \(B\) is single-valued.
special_cases_latex: For a shared variable represented by copies \(x_i\), consensus constraints \(x_1=\cdots=x_m\) can be incorporated through the normal cone of the consensus subspace.
A separable convex minimization problem is obtained from \(0\in\partial(\sum_i f_i)(x)\) after an appropriate product-space consensus lifting.
immediate_consequences_latex: The solution set can be studied through zeros of one operator on the product Hilbert space.
Locality requires each agent to evaluate \(A_i\) and its accessible portion of \(B_i\), but does not itself guarantee a distributed implementation.
boundary_notes: The definition does not assert that a solution exists or is unique.
Nonmonotone games and stochastic inclusions require separate qualifications not imposed here.

notation.meaning: The zero set \(\{x:0\in T(x)\}\) of a set-valued operator.

knowledge_statements.title: Distributed monotone-inclusion equilibrium problem
Distributed Variational Inequalities
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite set of agents holding separate operator components seek one feasible point whose aggregate operator has a nonnegative inner product with every feasible displacement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m,d\in\mathbb{N}\), let \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let agent \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\) hold a map \(F_i:K\to\mathbb{R}^d\). Given weights \(w_i>0\) satisfying \(\sum_{i=1}^{m}w_i=1\), define \(F=\sum_{i=1}^{m}w_iF_i\). The distributed variational inequality is to find \(x^\star\in K\) such that
\[\left\langle F(x^\star),z-x^\star\right\rangle\ge0\quad\text{for every }z\in K.\]
The model is distributed when agent \(i\) accesses only \(F_i\) or its oracle and the agents coordinate to obtain the common solution \(x^\star\).
assumptions_latex: \(m,d\in\mathbb{N}\).
\(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^\star\) solves \(\operatorname{VI}(K,\sum_{i=1}^{m}w_iF_i)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional variational inequality whose operator or feasible-set information is distributed among networked agents.

notation.meaning: operator component held by agent i

knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Monotone Inclusions
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite set of agents holding monotone operators seek a shared point where the sum of their operator values and the normal cone enforcing common feasibility contains zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m\in\mathbb{N}\), let \(\mathcal H\) be a real Hilbert space, let agent \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\) hold a set-valued monotone operator \(A_i:\mathcal H\rightrightarrows\mathcal H\), and let \(C\subseteq\mathcal H\) be nonempty, closed, and convex. A distributed monotone inclusion seeks
\[x^\star\in\mathcal H\quad\text{such that}\quad 0\in\sum_{i=1}^{m}A_i(x^\star)+N_C(x^\star).\]
Each agent accesses only its own operator or an available local resolvent. With local copies \(x_i\), consensus imposes the common-variable requirement, while \(N_C\) incorporates the shared feasibility constraint.
assumptions_latex: \(m\in\mathbb{N}\).
Each \(A_i\) is monotone; maximal monotonicity may additionally be imposed by a splitting method.
\(C\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^\star\in\operatorname{zer}(\sum_{i=1}^{m}A_i+N_C)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Common-zero monotone inclusion assembled from agent-local operators and an optional shared constraint.

notation.meaning: monotone operator held by agent i
normal-cone operator of the shared feasible set
zero set of a set-valued operator

knowledge_statements.title: Network Equilibrium Problems
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A network equilibrium is a feasible strategy profile at which no agent can lower its cost by a feasible unilateral deviation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For agents \(i=1,\ldots,m\), let \(x_i\in X_i\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{d_i}\), let \(J_i(x_i,x_{-i})\) be agent \(i\)'s cost, and let \(K_i(x_{-i})\subseteq X_i\) be its feasible-response set. A network equilibrium is a profile \(x^\star\) satisfying
\[x_i^\star\in K_i(x_{-i}^\star),\qquad J_i(x_i^\star,x_{-i}^\star)\le J_i(u_i,x_{-i}^\star)\quad\text{for every }u_i\in K_i(x_{-i}^\star),\]
for every agent \(i\). Network structure restricts each cost, constraint, and information exchange to specified neighbors, except for explicitly shared coupling constraints.
assumptions_latex: Each strategy set \(X_i\) is nonempty.
Each feasible-response set \(K_i(x_{-i})\) is specified by local, neighbor, or shared constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^\star\) is a generalized Nash equilibrium of the network-coupled game.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generalized Nash equilibrium with agent objectives and feasibility sets coupled through a network.

notation.meaning: strategies of all agents other than i

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The displayed generalized-Nash definition is mathematically plausible, but the only citation is a variational-inequality section and the candidate itself flags that the network-game formulation is only indirectly supported. A direct generalized-Nash or network-game source is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Equilibrium Coupling Structures
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A shared equilibrium constraint set can combine agent-local restrictions, pairwise edge constraints, and an aggregate resource constraint, with each class imposing a different coordination requirement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\) be an interaction graph, let \(x=(x_i)_{i\in V}\), and let \(X_i\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{d_i}\). For every \((i,j)\in E\), let \(c_{ij}:\mathbb{R}^{d_i}\times\mathbb{R}^{d_j}\to\mathbb{R}^{p_{ij}}\); let \(A_i:\mathbb{R}^{d_i}\to\mathbb{R}^{p}\) be linear; and let \(b\in\mathbb{R}^{p}\). A shared joint constraint set may be represented as
\[K=\left\{x:\ x_i\in X_i\ (i\in V),\quad c_{ij}(x_i,x_j)\le0\ ((i,j)\in E),\quad \sum_{i\in V}A_ix_i\le b\right\}.\]
The three displayed classes are agent-local, edgewise, and aggregate constraints, respectively. Removing either coupling class yields a corresponding local-only or reduced-coupling structure.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) specifies the interacting agent pairs.
\(X_i\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{d_i}\), \(c_{ij}\) takes values in \(\mathbb{R}^{p_{ij}}\), and every \(A_i\) takes values in a common space \(\mathbb{R}^{p}\).
All vector inequalities are interpreted componentwise.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K\) separates local, edgewise, and aggregate coupling in a shared equilibrium constraint set.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representation of local, edgewise, and aggregate coupling in network equilibrium models with a shared joint constraint set.

notation.meaning: vector constraint coupling neighboring agents i and j
linear map giving agent i's aggregate-resource contribution
